question: How much will Gold Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: This is a pure dispersion question: the mean of a 10-trading-day gold-minus-equity return difference is near zero and the answer is almost entirely about spread width. GVZ ~27 and VIX ~17.6 (mid-Sep 2026) imply a 10-day spread sigma of ~5.2-5.4pp, so I centered on a reference class of rolling 10-day gold-vs-S&P futures return differences and widened rather than narrowed. Center is essentially flat with a hair of positive tilt: gold is +19% y/y vs S&P ~+15%, just bounced off a six-week low with its first weekly gain in four, and late-Sep/early-Oct equity seasonality plus pre-midterm hedging are live -- offset almost exactly by the hawkish Warsh Fed (hiked to 3.75-4.00%, another hike telegraphed), a firmer dollar, falling oil, and gold's own eight-month downtrend from the January record. No human market prices this spread (Kalshi gold weeklies/GOLDPERP are level contracts, not relative-return contracts), so no crowd anchor was applied. Both bounds are open and sigma is ~5.4, putting ~3% of normal mass past each +/-10 edge before fat tails; I priced 4% below (gold capitulation on a hot payrolls print / real-yield spike while equities rally) and 5% above (risk-off or safe-haven spike where gold rises and equities fall together, the mechanism that historically generates the largest positive spreads). Payrolls on Oct 2 at 8:30 ET lands inside the window and adds a final-day shock that argues against trimming the tails.
sources: CBOE Gold ETF Volatility Index (GVZ), readings 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-17

calls.reasoning: Reference class: all 10-trading-day windows of (front-month gold futures % return minus E-mini S&P 500 futures % return), which is near-symmetric with a median of ~0 - there is no reliable two-week drift in either direction, so the base rate anchor is 0.0pp and the work is all in the spread. The current regime sets that spread wide: gold implied vol at 26.5 is 2x its 2013-19 norm and equity implied vol at 15.4 is low, giving a 10-day SD of the difference near 5.3-5.5pp - far wider than the ~2.5-3pp the same computation gives in a calm regime. 2026 itself confirms it: gold minus S&P diverged ~+23pp from January to mid-April and ~-31pp from mid-April to mid-September. Direction is a genuine coin flip. Gold-negative: a hawkish 25bp hike on Sep 16 with more priced, 30y yields above 5.2%, DXY at a 7-week high, oil retreating on the restored Saudi East-West pipeline, and gold sitting near the top of a $4,300-4,530 range after a 2-3% weekly bounce. Gold-positive: unresolved Middle East crisis, inflation still 'extremely high' per Warsh, VIX 15.4 with 91st-percentile 3-month call skew, late-September equity seasonality, and quarter-end rebalancing out of a strong equity quarter. I set the median at +0.1 and EV at +0.3 for the mild right skew gold carries in a geopolitical-risk regime - tilts well inside noise. Both open bounds get 4%: a Middle East escalation (gold up, equities down) on the high side, a continuation of the 2026 gold unwind into an equity melt-up on the low side; a normal with SD 5.3 gives ~3% each and fat tails justify rounding up. No prediction market prices this contract - checked Polymarket, Manifold, and Kalshi; Kalshi's annual S&P-vs-gold matchup (~65% S&P, late May) differs on horizon, instrument and threshold, so it is evidence, not an anchor. No shutdown risk inside the window (CR signed Sep 2 runs to Dec 11), but PCE on Sep 25, quarter-end, and the Oct 2 jobs report at 8:30 ET all land inside it, so realized vol should track implied rather than decay post-FOMC.

calls.reconciliation: Disputes were mostly stale-timestamp artifacts, not real conflicts. GVZ: 26.54 confirmed by two independent runs; Run 3's competing 16.16 sits below the same source's stated 252-day low of 16.38, so it cannot be a current print - discarded. VIX: 15.44 vs 17.62 could not be settled without web access (Now is 14:34 ET, so no Sep 18 close exists yet); I carried the 15-18 band, which moves the spread SD by only ~0.2pp. Gold spot quotes ($4,309 / $4,388 / $4,421) and Brent quotes ($103-104 / $98.46) are different timestamps within the same moves, not contradictions, and levels are irrelevant to a relative-return question. All three runs independently confirmed: no FOMC inside the window, CR to Dec 11 removing shutdown risk, PCE ~Sep 25, quarter-end Sep 30, NFP Oct 2 08:30 ET ahead of the 20:00Z resolution, and no matching prediction market. The resolution convention (start mark, contract month) was unfound by all three and stays unsettled; it adds dispersion rather than subtracting it. I did not carry any run's dispersion figure verbatim - I rebuilt the SD from the realized daily moves reported in the dossiers and cross-checked it against the implied-vol computation, landing at 5.3pp, inside all three runs' 5.0-5.5 range. The only place I stepped outside all three was the median (0.0 vs their +0.1/+0.2/+0.3): pure judgment, no evidence breaks the tie, and I weight equities' positive ten-day drift plus the uniformly gold-negative macro cluster as cancelling gold's two-day bounce.
